layout_dets.text: Improved Ferritic-Austenitic Stainless Steel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by W. H. Richardson and P. Guha

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Langley Alloys Limited, Langley, Slough, Berkshire

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Manuscript received 1 November, 1978; revised manuscript 20 June, 1979)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For the efficient operation of chemical process plant it is of paramount importance to ensure as far as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: possible that the periods of closure for maintenance and repair are minimised.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The arduous conditions encountered in many chemical plants as a result of progressive trends towards

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: higher yields, etc., have therefore highlighted the need for greater strength and pitting resistance than can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be ·obtained in conventional austenitic stainless steels. This paper describes the development of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ferritic/austenitic high chromium duplex cast stainless steels and demonstrates how, by addition of nitrogen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and close control of composition, certain inherent drawbacks of duplex alloys can be overcome. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nitrogen-containing steel has an attractive combination of mechanical properties, corrosion resistance,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ductility, weldability and castability, and has received application in a wide range of aggressive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: environments.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: AUSTENITIC stainless steels have long been known for their

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: good corrosion resistance and have been extensively used in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chemical plants. The development of chemical and other process

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plants has seen progressive trends towards achieving high yield,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: often requiring high concentrations and higher temperatures

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which lead to the shortening of service life of the stainless steels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: commonly used. This can lead to costly inspection and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maintenance involving production loss due to plant shut down,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and has been recently highlighted.1

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Conventional austenitic stainless steels are inherently low

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: strength alloys, and can suffer from pitting and crevice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion in the presence of chloride ions, due to localised

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: breakdown of the passivating surface film. These alloys are also

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prone to stress corrosion cracking in chloride environments. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: choice of a suitable material to combat the more severe

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conditions in chemical plants and in marine environments such

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as North Sea Oil Fields is therefore difficult.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The search for suitable alternatives has led to the development

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of high chromium duplex ferritic/austenitic steels and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interest in such stainless steels for use in chemical and marine

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: industries has increased during the past 10 years. This paper

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: details comparative mechanical and corrosion characteristics of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two such steels:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (1) A.C.I. CD-4MCu Alloy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (2) FERRALIUM Alloy*

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: High Chromium-Ferritic-Austenitic Steels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: High chromium-ferritic-austenitic steels are known to have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: good corrosion resistance. The effect of high chromium in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improving general corrosion resistance has been reported by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: various authors,2-4 and the beneficial effect of high chromium

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: content on pitting resistance in chloride environments has also

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been reported.s,6 High chromium low carbon alloys, however,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are generally coarse grained and brittle. Due to their inherent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lack of ductility, propensity to cracking, and certain fabrication

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: problems,47 application of these alloys has in practice been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: severely restricted.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The development of a high chromium duplex steel CD-4MCu

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with additions of molybdenum and copper was reported by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fontana8 in 1956. This alloy was later incorporated in an Alloy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Casting Institute data sheet under the same code name. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: results reported indicated good general corrosion resistance,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stress corrosion resistance and high strength. Attempts to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: produce castings of heavy or variable section, however, proved

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to be very difficult due to cracking problems and this alloy was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: also found to be prone to thermal cracking during heat

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: treatment.9 Brautingan¹º also highlighted these shortcomings,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and a modified heat treatment schedule, both complex and time-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consuming, had to be devised to overcome this tendency to ther-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mal cracking. Published information and production experience

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of A.C.I. CD-4MCu alloy indicate that this alloy still largely

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: suffers from the inherent drawbacks of the previously known

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: high chromium duplex steels. The percentage composition range

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of A.C.I. CD-4MCu alloy is as follows: Cr 25-26.5; Ni

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Development of Improved Alloy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It was clearly desirable to develop an alloy possessing the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: good corrosion characteristics of duplex steels but having

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: markedly improved mechanical properties, castability and weld-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ability, yielding a general purpose alloy having wide acceptance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and application in the chemical engineering industry.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It is well known that nitrogen additions can improve the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: strength of fully austenitic steels" as well as being an austenite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stabiliser. It was therefore decided to investigate the effects of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adding nitrogen to duplex ferritic-austenitic steels, an area not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: previously investigated. In order to retain the good stress

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion and pitting resistance of the steels of duplex structure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it was necessary to study also the effects of varying chromium

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and nickel contents over a wide range so that the appropriate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloy contents for a given nitrogen addition could be optimised

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to retain the duplex structure. In practice, as indicated below, a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: surprising outcome of this work was not only that a marked

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improvement in ductility was obtained but also that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion resistance of the duplex steels was improved by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nitrogen additions. The resultant nitrogen-containing alloy is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: now widely accepted for use in marine and chemical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: environments.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Results and Discussion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Alloys were produced as castings and hot rolled bar having

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nominal compositions of 1.5-3.5% copper, 2.5% molybdenum

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with varying chromium and nickel contents in the ranges

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 23–27% and 4.0–6.5%, respectively, and with nitrogen contents

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the range 0.05-0.22% (Table I). Steels with copper at the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lower end of the range were used for producing rolled bar.

layout_dets.text: Mechanical properties

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The mechanical properties of specimens from castings, shown

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Table I, demonstrate the beneficial effect of nitrogen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: additions, for duplex steels containing about 25% chromium,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5% nickel, 3% copper and 2.5% molybdenum. The low impact

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: properties and ductility of the essentially nitrogen-free alloys are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: particularly striking in heat treated and thick sections.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Table II illustrates the effect of varying chromium content on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the mechanical properties of the duplex nitrogen-containing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels. It is seen that an increase in chromium content can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adversely affect the ductility of these steels, but that this can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: largely overcome by an appropriate increase in nitrogen content.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Corrosion characteristics

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The corrosion characteristics of duplex steels were studied

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using both potentiostatic and immersion (weight loss) test

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods. Potentiostatic polarisation studies were carried out

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: according to the ASTM G1 Committee recommendations; all

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potentials quoted are with reference to the saturated calomel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: electrode (SCE). The effect of 16 h immersion periods on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion/pitting current density at +600 mV was also studied.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The cell arrangement and electrode holder for these experiments

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were as recommended by Greene.12

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 1 illustrates the effect of varying chromium content on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the pitting current densities on steels containing approximately

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5% nickel, 3% copper, 2.5% molybdenum and 0.15% nitrogen.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It is seen that a minimum chromium content of about 24.5% is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: desirable in order to ensure that satisfactory passivity is retained

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the presence of chloride ions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 2 shows the effect of varying nickel content on the pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: behaviour of steels containing approximately 25% chromium,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3% copper and 2.5% molybdenum. It is seen that the nickel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: should be maintained within a fairly narrow range, of about

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.7–6·0%, in order to obtain optimum pitting resistance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As indicated earlier, nitrogen was added to duplex steels in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: order to achieve an improved combination of mechanical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: properties. Surprisingly, a marked improvement in corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance properties was also achieved, as shown in Fig. 3,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where the potentiostatic polarisation characteristics in 3% NaCl

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compared with 0.05% in alloy 6. It is seen that a significant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improvement in breakdown/pitting potential is achieved by the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: On the basis of the mechanical and corrosion resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: properties described above it was possible to characterise a new

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloy, having the following preferred range of composition:

layout_dets.text: Chromium

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Balance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This alloy satisfied, in laboratory tests, the target require-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ments for corrosion characteristics, showing in fact significant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improvement over CD—4MCu, combined with very satisfactory

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: strength and ductility.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Production experience during the past 15 years has confirmed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that this alloy does not suffer from the drawbacks of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conventional high chromium duplex alloys. The alloy can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: readily welded, without encountering any HAZ cracking and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: delayed cracking, often associated with other high chromium

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: duplex alloys. Numerous weld fabricated castings and cast to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: Summary and Conclusions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The results described in this paper indicate that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FERRALIUM Alloy possesses an excellent combination of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mechanical properties and corrosion resistance. Stability of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: passivation film in the presence of chloride ions has also been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: demonstrated. To safeguard these important characteristics,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: control of composition and addition of nitrogen is of paramount

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: importance.
